lesson.summary: Understand summary from first principles, with a small runnable example.

stage.name: Object Tools & Design
stage.subtitle: Book chapters 5–6
stage.description: Namespaces, attributes, closures, generators, reflection, plus OOP design principles such as SOLID.

payload.markdown: In this chapter, I covered some of the techniques and tools that you can use to manage your libraries and classes. I explored PHP’s namespace feature. You saw that we can combine include paths, namespaces, autoload, and the file system to provide a flexible organization for classes. We also examined PHP’s object and class functions, before taking things to the next level with the powerful Reflection API. We used the Reflection classes to build a simple example that illustrates one of the potential uses that Reflection has to offer. Finally, we combined the Reflection classes with attributes: a major feature new to PHP 8.

items: Attributes: Structured metadata attached to classes and members, readable at runtime.
Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Functions: Reusable blocks of code that take arguments and return values.
HTTP & REST: Designing HTTP endpoints as resources with predictable methods and status codes.
Namespaces: Named scopes that prevent class-name collisions and organise code.
Reflection: Inspecting classes, methods and properties from running code.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Arrow Functions: fn() => expressions: closures with automatic by-value capture.
